methodologyNotes: Scope: 14 notable smart/motorized window-covering products a US buyer compares in 2026, spanning DIY retrofit tilt-only clips (SwitchBot Blind Tilt, RYSE SmartShade, SmarterHome/MySmartBlinds), DIY retrofit full-shade kits (IKEA FYRTUR, SwitchBot Roller Shade, Yoolax, Eve MotionBlinds, SmartWings Zebra Shades), premium dealer-installed lines (Lutron Serena, Hunter Douglas PowerView Gen 3, Graber Virtual Cord, Levolor InMotion, Bali Motorization), and a bare motor component sold through the dealer channel (Somfy Sonesse Ultra 30 WireFree). Two seeds were corrected against current reality: 'SwitchBot Roller Shade 3' does not exist as a SKU -- SwitchBot's current roller-shade product is simply named 'Roller Shade' (used here); 'Zebra Motorized Blinds' turned out to be zebrablinds.com, a multi-brand retailer (it resells Graber and Norman, not a house-brand motor) -- replaced with SmartWings, a real motorized zebra-shade product line a buyer actually finds when shopping this category. 'SmarterHome Motorized' is SmarterHome's MySmartBlinds Automation Kit (SmarterHome acquired the MySmartBlinds brand). specKeys were expanded from the 9 suggested to 11: added hub_required (whether a separate bridge/gateway purchase is mandatory to unlock voice/app/remote control -- the single biggest practical differentiator in this category) and installation_type (retrofit clip-on vs standalone replacement shade vs bare motor component), since these drive the actual buying decision as much as raw specs. motor_noise_db is left null for the majority of products because manufacturers rarely publish an absolute SPL rating; the two populated values (Graber 9.6dB, Yoolax 48dB, Somfy 42dB, SwitchBot Roller Shade 30dB) come from a lab-style measurement (TechHive) or a manufacturer-stated rating -- not comparable to each other without knowing test methodology, noted per-product in provenance. Research constraints: this session's WebSearch quota was exhausted partway through, so remaining research used direct WebFetch plus two workarounds for JS-heavy or bot-walled sites -- the DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint (html.duckduckgo.com/html) as a search substitute, and the r.jina.ai read-proxy to render JavaScript-rendered product pages (ikea.com, yoolax.com, switch-bot.com, helloryse.com, evehome.com, somfysystems.com, levolor.com, baliblinds.com, serenashades.com/smarterhome.com partially) that returned 403/429 to a direct fetch. IKEA.com and Lutron's serenashades.com CDN block automated fetches outright even via the proxy for image bytes (curl gets a Varnish/Akamai 403), so those two products' prices and specs are sourced from reputable secondary coverage (gearbrain.com, apalrd.net hands-on review, myintelligenthouse.com dealer price chart, support.lutron.com FAQ) rather than the manufacturer page directly -- flagged in each product's provenance. Lutron, Hunter Douglas, Graber, Levolor, and Bali are dealer-priced custom products with no fixed public MSRP; priceUsd reflects the smallest/base published configuration from a named retailer or dealer price chart, not a universal price, and priceNote says so explicitly. Somfy's Sonesse Ultra 30 is a bare motor component installed inside a made-to-measure shade by a workroom -- its price is for the motor alone, not a finished window covering. One product (SmarterHome MySmartBlinds Automation Kit) ships without an image field: no Wikimedia Commons file exists for it and every manufacturer/retailer product photo url found (smarterhome.com, sophisticatedtools.com) sat behind bot-blocking that also blocked image byte retrieval -- omitted rather than guessed, per the null-beats-a-guess rule. All other images were downloaded and verified as real image bytes (correct magic number, plausible product-shot dimensions) before being included; none are Wikimedia Commons files because a Commons media-search API check (api.php action=query&list=search against commons.wikimedia.org) returned zero hits for every product/brand pairing in this category -- these window-covering products are too niche/recent to have been photographed for Commons. accessedAt = 2026-08-01 for every source/corroboration/image in this file.
